jobs.description:
Senior SSA Enterprise Systems Program Manager and Technology Advisor

Function: Enterprise Technology Strategy, Program Management, and Federal Information Technology Advisory
Location: Remote

Reports to: Executive Leadership

POSITION SUMMARY

We are seeking a senior technology leader, program manager, or technical advisor with substantial experience supporting Social Security Administration (SSA) technology programs, systems, organizations, or enterprise services. Relevant experience may have been gained as an SSA employee or as a contractor, subcontractor, consultant, or industry partner directly supporting SSA technology work.

The successful candidate may bring broad enterprise experience across multiple SSA technology domains or deep expertise within a major technical domain, supported by sufficient familiarity with related areas to advise leadership and coordinate complex delivery. Relevant domains include software and web development, database and data administration, software engineering, systems integration, cloud services, infrastructure, systems administration, cybersecurity, enterprise architecture, and digital services.

This position combines strategic advisory responsibilities with hands-on enterprise program management. The individual must understand SSA’s technology environment, organizational structure, operating practices, stakeholder relationships, and contractor-supported services and be able to translate that knowledge into actionable plans, independent assessments, executive materials, risk management, stakeholder coordination, and practical recommendations that move initiatives from strategy through execution.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead and coordinate complex enterprise technology initiatives from planning through execution, including the development of work plans, schedules, priorities, deliverables, decision points, and performance measures.
  • Provide executive-level guidance while directly managing assigned activities, developing work products, tracking actions, and driving issues through resolution.
  • Advise leadership on SSA technology organizations, governance structures, decision-making processes, stakeholder roles, technical dependencies, and contractor relationships.
  • Translate strategic objectives and leadership direction into practical plans, clearly defined activities, accountable owners, timelines, and measurable outcomes.
  • Coordinate with executive, program, technical, operational, acquisition, security, and contractor stakeholders to maintain alignment and support timely decision-making.
  • Apply direct knowledge of SSA’s technology environment, systems, operating practices, organizational expectations, and contractor-supported services when evaluating proposed approaches.
  • Review technical, staffing, governance, transition, and operating approaches for alignment with established practices, systems, security requirements, organizational constraints, and delivery expectations.
  • Independently evaluate proposed technical architectures, delivery approaches, dependencies, risks, and implementation feasibility across software and web development, database and data administration, software engineering, systems integration, cloud, infrastructure, systems administration, cybersecurity, enterprise architecture, and digital services.
  • Provide senior subject matter expertise within one or more major SSA technology domains while maintaining sufficient enterprise awareness to assess dependencies and impacts across related areas.
  • Identify, document, and manage technical, operational, organizational, integration, staffing, schedule, and transition risks that could affect delivery.
  • Develop and maintain program management materials, including implementation plans, schedules, action trackers, risk and issue logs, decision papers, status reports, operating procedures, and performance dashboards.
  • Review proposed program leadership, technical leadership, team structures, escalation paths, reporting relationships, and governance processes.
  • Lead or support large-scale technical transitions, incumbent workforce continuity, knowledge transfer, credentialing, system access, onboarding, and operational readiness activities.
  • Provide guidance regarding multi-vendor delivery, contractor performance, key personnel, staffing models, technical dependencies, Government oversight, and division of responsibilities among participating organizations.
  • Assess whether proposed staffing and technical approaches include the appropriate experience, domain expertise, leadership capability, and institutional knowledge needed to perform successfully within the SSA environment.
  • Develop and review executive briefings, technical narratives, management approaches, transition strategies, staffing plans, operating procedures, and performance frameworks.
  • Facilitate leadership discussions, working sessions, technical reviews, solution assessments, independent evaluations, and structured decision-making sessions.
  • Provide candid, practical recommendations based on direct SSA experience and follow through on resulting decisions, actions, and deliverables.
  • Help leadership distinguish between approaches that appear credible in written proposals and those that are realistically executable within SSA’s technical, organizational, security, acquisition, and operational environment.

BASIC JOB REQUIREMENTS

  • Must have substantial direct experience supporting SSA technology programs, systems, organizations, or enterprise services.
  • SSA experience may have been gained as an SSA employee or as a contractor, subcontractor, consultant, or industry partner directly supporting SSA technology work.
  • General federal information technology experience without meaningful direct SSA technology experience will not satisfy this requirement.
  • Must have served in a senior technology leadership, enterprise program management, technical advisory, technical delivery, program director, technical director, systems leadership, or comparable role.
  • Must possess either broad experience across software and web development, database and data administration, software engineering, systems integration, cloud, infrastructure, systems administration, cybersecurity, enterprise architecture, and digital services, or deep expertise in one or more of these domains with working familiarity across the related technical and operational areas.
  • Must have demonstrated experience managing or supporting complex technology programs or initiatives, including planning, execution, stakeholder coordination, risk management, performance tracking, and executive reporting.
  • Must understand how SSA technology organizations, program offices, technical teams, acquisition personnel, security organizations, Government leaders, and contractors interact.
  • Must have experience supporting or overseeing large-scale technology services, technical programs, contractors, subcontractors, or multi-vendor delivery environments.
  • Must possess strong knowledge of federal technology governance, organizational structures, technical decision-making, stakeholder responsibilities, and contractor interaction.
  • Must have experience evaluating technical delivery, program performance, quality, schedule, risk, staffing, resources, key personnel, or contractor performance.
  • Must be able to assess technical and management approaches from both a domain-specific and enterprise perspective and translate that assessment into actionable recommendations and executable plans.
  • Must be able to develop high-quality program plans, executive briefings, decision materials, status reports, risk assessments, operating procedures, technical narratives, and other management deliverables.
  • Must be able to operate independently, manage competing priorities, organize ambiguous requirements, and move complex activities forward with limited direction.
  • Must be comfortable advising executive leadership while also taking direct responsibility for planning, coordination, analysis, documentation, tracking, and delivery.
  • Experience serving as or working closely with an SSA executive, Government program manager, Contracting Officer’s Representative, Contracting Officer’s Technical Representative, technical director, program director, system owner, division director, or senior information technology official is strongly preferred.
  • Experience supporting SSA modernization, cloud, cybersecurity, data, infrastructure, digital services, enterprise architecture, systems integration, application development, incumbent transition, credentialing, or access continuity is strongly preferred.
  • Experience supporting major SSA contracts, enterprise technology services, contractor transitions, proposal development, technical evaluations, or program startup activities is preferred.
  • Experience advising senior leadership while directly managing major technology programs, contractor-supported services, organizational change, or enterprise transformation is preferred.

jobs.excerpt: GHX is a healthcare supply chain exchange.  At its core, what we do is move transaction data reliably between thousands of trading partners.
jobs.description:
GHX is a healthcare supply chain exchange. At its core, what we do is move transaction data reliably between thousands of trading partners. Integration and data architecture are not supporting concerns here; they are central to how our product works and how we scale.

This role owns the long-term stewardship of both problems: how data is modeled, accessed, and owned within our services, and how it flows reliably across them. You will work directly with application teams as a hands-on technical partner and architect, setting technical direction, establishing integration and data patterns, and ensuring the architectural quality we build today does not become tomorrow's maintenance burden. Your peers are strong backend engineers building real products. You earn trust through depth and direct engagement, not architecture diagrams from a distance.

What You'll Do

Integration Architecture & Event-Driven Systems

  • Define GHX's integration patterns: outbox, saga, CDC, event-carried state transfer, dual-write mitigation, and when to choreograph vs. orchestrate
  • Guide service boundary design: where to draw domain lines, how to handle shared reference data, and how to prevent shared-database coupling between services
  • Own the messaging and eventing layer: topic and queue design, schema contracts, partitioning, retention, consumer group management, dead-letter handling, replay, and operational monitoring
  • Lead the architectural direction for replacing GHX's homegrown event bus with a cloud-native messaging platform, and establish the standards teams will build on after the transition
  • Guide teams on streaming vs. batch trade-offs and on replacing batch- or file-driven pipelines with event-driven flows where latency and reliability require it

API Design, Contracts & DevOps

  • Establish REST API design standards: resource modeling, versioning strategy, error contracts, pagination, and backward compatibility
  • Own the API governance lifecycle: versioning policy, deprecation timelines, breaking change detection in CI/CD, schema compatibility enforcement, and consumer-driven contract testing
  • Define traffic management patterns for API transitions: versioned routing, canary rollouts, and gateway configuration for safe rollout and rollback
  • Guide teams on integration style selection and review service designs for evolvability and downstream interface cost

Data Architecture & Database Practice

  • Work with teams on schema design, data modeling, and aligning data ownership with service boundaries
  • Guide datastore selection by workload: read/write patterns, consistency requirements, and cost trade-offs across relational, document, key-value, and analytical options; for NoSQL, lead access-pattern-first design including partition strategy, secondary index selection, and partition distribution
  • Advise on ORM vs. raw query trade-offs and define data access standards that avoid common anti-patterns (N+1, chatty calls, unbounded result sets)
  • Guide teams on performant data access and zero-downtime schema evolution: indexing strategy, backfill approaches, dual-write windows, and rollback-safe migrations
  • Establish replication and syndication patterns for cross-service data movement: CDC, change streams, materialized views, and read models

Enablement & Standards

  • Run design reviews, workshops, and office hours to raise integration and data fundamentals across engineering
  • Produce decision records, design guides, and reference implementations teams can build from
  • Present architectural trade-offs and technical risk to engineering leadership, product, and senior stakeholders

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years building distributed systems, grounded in hands-on software development as an individual contributor: you have written and shipped production code and understand the day-to-day engineering reality your guidance needs to hold up against
  • Deep experience with event-driven architecture and distributed systems: pub/sub and messaging infrastructure (Kafka, AWS SQS/SNS/EventBridge, or equivalents), integration patterns (outbox, CDC, saga, event sourcing), and failure modes including idempotency, consistency trade-offs, and operational failure handling
  • Hands-on AWS experience with data and integration services: SQS, SNS, EventBridge, DynamoDB, RDS/Aurora, API Gateway, Lambda
  • Strong data architecture fundamentals across relational and NoSQL: datastore selection by workload, schema and access-pattern design, ORM trade-offs, and performant data access at scale
  • Experience designing REST APIs with attention to versioning, backward compatibility, and data contracts, including contract validation in CI/CD pipelines
  • Experience working directly with application teams during service decomposition, and a track record of establishing integration and data standards across an engineering organization
  • Strong communication across levels: writing clear decision records for engineering peers, presenting trade-offs to engineering and product leadership, and translating technical risk for senior stakeholders
  • Heavy personal investment in AI-assisted and agentic development: your workflow has materially changed over the last 6-12 months, you use coding agents for substantial engineering work, and you have concrete examples of where these tools have made you meaningfully faster or produced better outcomes; the engineers around you tend to notice and follow

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience integrating with external partners or enterprise platforms (supply chain, ERP, CRM, or similar), including migrating from batch- or file-driven pipelines to event-driven flows
  • Healthcare or other regulated industry experience
  • Azure PaaS experience (Service Bus, Cosmos DB, Azure Functions)
  • Infrastructure-as-code experience (Terraform or equivalents)
  • Analytics data layer experience: Snowflake, Redshift, or similar
  • Data architecture for ML/LLM applications (vector databases, embeddings, RAG patterns)
  • Prior Principal or Staff Engineer experience

What We're Looking For

You grew up as a developer. You have written the code, debugged the query plan that fell apart at scale, and been on call when a consumer queue fell behind. That experience is what makes architectural guidance credible, and what keeps decisions grounded in the reality of building and operating software. You have worked through the hard problems in distributed systems: service boundaries that do not hold, shared databases that create invisible coupling, async pipelines that fail in ways the original design never anticipated. You bring depth in both the integration layer and the data layer, and you know from experience how problems in one become problems in the other.

You are a hands-on architect who succeeds by making other engineers better. You can design the event contract, identify the breaking change in an API proposal before it ships, and dig into an operational failure when it matters. You write clear decision records, give direct feedback in design reviews, and know when to push back and when to ship. You also communicate well outside engineering: you can present a build-vs-buy decision to an executive, work through a data model with a product manager, and explain reliability risk to a business stakeholder without losing the thread.

Why This Role Matters

GHX is in the middle of a significant architectural transformation: decomposing a large-scale monolith into independently deployable services. The integration and data architecture decisions made during this transition will shape how we build and operate systems for the next decade. Getting it right is what separates genuine team autonomy from coupling that has simply moved into a distributed form.

Beyond the transformation, this is a permanent leadership function. The person in this role will define the technical character of how GHX connects its systems, set standards that persist as the organization scales, and be a direct partner to engineering leadership on the most consequential architectural decisions we make.

Estimated Salary Range for this position: $150,000 to $214,000 plus bonus

The base salary range represents the anticipated low and high end of the GHX’s salary range for this position. The base salary is one component of GHX’s total compensation package for employees. Other rewards and benefits include: health, vision, and dental insurance, accident and life insurance, 401k matching, paid-time off, and education reimbursement, to name a few. To view more details of our benefits, visit us here:

GHX: It's the way you do business in healthcare

We're so happy you're here! Thank you for checking our job out and we hope to have the chance to meet you in our interview process!

About the role

We're hiring a Senior Retail Operations Specialist to run the daily engine behind Grüns retail fulfillment. You'll ensure every order ships accurately, on time, and in full - protecting revenue, keeping retail partners happy, and catching problems before they become costly. This role connects internal ops, 3PLs, and retail accounts, and owns the proactive inventory and OTIF work that keeps our retail business scaling cleanly. This role reports to our Director of Retail Operations.

This role is part of our remote HQ! We have a fully remote, high-trust work environment - and also come together on a biannual basis for amazing off-sites where we can connect IRL.

In this role, you will:

  • Own day-to-day retail order fulfillment, monitoring and resolving "where's my product" issues before they turn into late or incomplete shipments.
  • Proactively manage base inventory to get ahead of shortages - flagging risk before orders are shorted, not after.
  • Process new orders accurately and on schedule to keep product flowing without disruption.
  • Run proactive inventory reviews for promotions and new item launches to ensure plans execute cleanly.
  • Track OTIF performance, chargebacks, and late trucks, and drive the process improvements that move those numbers.
  • Manage 3PL and logistics partner relationships, resolving escalations and holding partners to SLA.
  • Build and document SOPs across retail ops - receiving, lot/expiry management, promotions, and returns - so the function scales with the business.
  • Identify tools (including AI) and workflow changes that make the role and the broader retail ops function more efficient.

We're looking for someone who:

  • Has 3+ years of experience in retail operations, order fulfillment, or replenishment in a CPG environment, with a genuinely analytical approach to the work.
  • Has direct experience with Walmart and Club channel (Sam's Club, Costco), and ideally distributors like UNFI or KeHE.
  • Understands EDI order management, lot codes, and expiration handling in a retail fulfillment context.
  • Is fluent in Excel or Google Sheets - pivot tables, VLOOKUPs, basic modeling - and comfortable with ERP/WMS systems (Fulfil.io a strong plus).
  • Communicates clearly and confidently with both internal teams and external retail/logistics partners.
  • Is comfortable using AI tools like Claude to move faster and think more clearly, not just check a box.
  • Has a track record of finding and fixing inefficiency, not just maintaining what exists.

Approach to the role:

  • Proactive - flags problems before they become fires, not after.
  • Organized under pressure - manages competing priorities without dropping the important ones.
  • Independent - doesn't need to be managed to stay ahead of the work.
  • Data-driven - makes the call based on facts, not assumptions.
  • Curious and iterative - always looking for a cleaner, faster way to do it.

Compensation & Benefits:

At Grüns, we're committed to providing a competitive total compensation package — grounded in market data that considers our size, stage, industry, and location. For this role, the base salary range is $90,000 - $100,000 plus bonus depending on experience, paired with a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the well-being and growth of our team.

A bit about us...

At Grüns, we believe that foundational nutrition should be simple and convenient for everyone. We're dedicated to bringing comprehensive and real nutrition to you through our gummies, formulated from 60 nutrient-dense and whole-food ingredients. Simply enjoy a grab-and-go snack pack of gummies daily whenever fits best in your schedule and wherever life takes you.

Like you, we were disappointed. There’s an infinite number of “nutrition” companies, all focused on what’s best for them — not what’s best for you. Hundreds of products to sell you on, low-quality ingredients, and small nutrient doses. We’ve seen it all.

So we decided it was time to fix it. No more choking on and popping pills like a pharmacy. No more clean-up and disgust from gross powders. And no more cobbling together handfuls to dozens of supplements. Grüns is comprehensive nutrition, made convenient and delicious.

What we care about...

Be the Best: We hold ourselves, our teams, and our partners to an incredibly high standard - and we raise the bar constantly. "We've never done this before" isn't an excuse here. It's an invitation.

Own It: We act like our name is on the door. That means taking complete ownership of outcomes, collaborating deeply, working through roadblocks - not around them - and never waiting for someone else to solve the problem. Great owners are great partners.

Drive Impact, Urgently: We measure impact, not effort. We work smart and hard, move fast, and use every tool at our disposal - including AI - to focus our energy where it matters most.

Compensation & Perks:

For every role, we aim to have highly competitive compensation and opportunity for impact and career growth.

Everyone at Grüns works hard, but we believe in wellness and balance too. We have super strong benefits coverage -- for you and your family, generous PTO, free Grüns subscriptions, and a few more perks centered around health and well-being that we can't wait to tell you about!

jobs.description:
Role Title: Military Writing Specialist

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote (US Only)

micro1 is engaging Military Writing Specialists to support a unique project, leveraging expertise in military writing and reporting. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters. Contributors will use their background in Department of War (Department of Defense) documentation to generate, review, and evaluate a wide range of reports, summaries, and status updates reflective of authentic military processes. Your input will help develop benchmarks and grading guidelines that will teach AI to understand and replicate effective, compliant government communication.

Scope of Work

  1. Create realistic military and federal status reports, summaries, and executive updates based on prompts and supplied artifacts.
  2. Develop “golden responses” that demonstrate high-quality, standards-aligned reporting for use in AI model training.
  3. Draft grading rubrics and guidelines that reflect best practices in federal and military writing assessment.
  4. Evaluate AI-generated reports, providing detailed feedback in both written and verbal form.
  5. Share context on stylistic differences and individual approaches to common military documents (e.g., WARs, SITREPs, AARs, executive summaries).
  6. Produce supporting documents such as decision briefs, memoranda, and action officer updates when required.
  7. Collaborate with other subject matter experts to ensure diversity of reporting styles and adherence to branch-specific terminology.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Former U.S. Department of War (Department of Defense) professional with at least 3 years of relevant experience.
  2. Experience producing templated and standard reports such as Weekly Activity Reports (WARs), Situation Reports (SITREPs), After-Action Reviews, or similar artifacts.
  3. Expertise spanning two or more branches of the U.S. military is a plus; a diverse background across roles is highly valued.
  4. Proven proficiency in written and verbal communication, particularly in conveying technical or operational subject matter.
  5. Demonstrated ability to craft, grade, and review back office documents, PowerPoints, memos, and spreadsheets for military or federal purposes.
  6. US-based contributor with broad familiarity with federal documentation standards and compliance best practices.
  7. Comfortable collaborating remotely and sharing insights on nuanced, highly procedural reporting tasks.

About Cardiac Care Alliance (CCA)

Cardiac Care Alliance is a Management Services Organization (MSO) committed to building a high-performance cardiovascular network. We partner with independent cardiologists to deliver value-based care (VBC) models that complement traditional fee-for-service delivery. Our mission is to improve patient access, clinical outcomes, and overall experience through proactive care coordination and evidence-based interventions.

Position Summary

CCA is hiring full-time virtual Care Coordinators to support a growing population of medically complex patients with cardiac conditions, primarily congestive heart failure (CHF). This role is integral to our population health initiatives — proactively supporting at-risk patients with data-informed outreach, continuity of care, and patient-centered engagement.

This role will focus on supporting Principal Care Management (PCM), Chronic Care Management (CCM), and Transitional Care Management (TCM) services via telephonic outreach and technology-enabled documentation platforms. Care Coordinators work collaboratively with a team of Registered Nurses and Cardiologists, escalating clinical concerns and complex care needs as appropriate.

This position does not require RN licensure, but candidates must have strong clinical acumen, attention to detail, and the ability to navigate complex care environments.

Key Responsibilities

  • Conduct structured telephonic outreach to CHF patients and other complex cardiac patients
  • Maintain a caseload of assigned patients, using risk stratification to prioritize care
  • Complete initial assessments and timely follow-ups addressing current symptoms, medication regimen and adherence, functional and psychosocial status
  • Assess home safety and social determinants of health (SDOH) barriers, including transportation, food insecurity, housing instability, and caregiver support; escalate resource needs where appropriate
  • Advance care planning needs and specialty care follow-up
  • Review and act on population health dashboards to address care gaps (annual wellness visits, missing labs, lack of symptom monitoring, etc.)
  • Provide ongoing patient education and promote evidence-based self-management strategies for CHF
  • Monitor for signs of worsening conditions or gaps in care, and escalate as needed
  • Support transitional care follow-up within 48 hours post-discharge, focusing on medication reconciliation, red-flag symptom screening, and appointment scheduling
  • Document time, interventions, care plans, and patient goals in the care management platform in alignment with CMS billing standards
  • Maintain proactive communication with RNs, Cardiologists, PCP offices, and other clinical partners

Scope of Work – Limitations

This role is non-clinical in license and does not include:

  • Clinical assessment or medical diagnosis
  • Medication prescribing or adjustments
  • Interpretation of diagnostic results (labs, imaging, EKGs, etc.)
  • Clinical triage or emergency response
  • Home visits or in-person patient contact
  • Billing or coding responsibilities beyond required documentation

All clinical decision-making, care plan authorization, and treatment recommendations are made by licensed providers and/or supervising RNs.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Active Medical Assistant (MA) certification or equivalent clinical credential (e.g., CNA, EMT, CHW with experience)
  • Minimum 2 years of experience in care coordination, case management, or ambulatory care
  • Strong interpersonal communication skills and ability to build rapport by phone
  • Familiarity with CMS PCM, CCM, and/or TCM program requirements
  • Technologically proficient with care coordination software or EHRs
  • Ability to work independently and efficiently in a remote environment

We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. We are looking for a Senior Technical Recruiter (Global) to drive hiring across Engineering, Product, Data, AI, Infrastructure, and other technical functions globally.

This role combines hands-on recruitment execution with leadership responsibilities. You will be responsible for attracting top technical talent, partnering with senior stakeholders on hiring strategy, and helping build a high-performing Talent Acquisition function as the company continues to scale globally.

jobs.description:
• Location: Remote — U.S.-based required. For this opening we give preference to candidates based in the Central or Mountain time zones; all zones are considered if the coverage window below genuinely works for your life.

  • Reports to: Head of Sales

About Breathe for Change

Breathe for Change (B4C) is building the category of Human Intelligence in Education to address the crises of educator stress and burnout, student mental health, and AI disruption. Our accredited higher-education programs — anchored by our Master's of Education — equip educators with the human skills they and their students need most to thrive. We envision a world where school is about what truly matters: empowering students AND teachers to live purposeful, creative lives full of vitality, wholeness, and connection.

The role

You'll be a full-cycle inside sales professional guiding teachers through the decision to enroll in B4C's degree programs. Marketing fills your calendar with booked 1:1 phone calls — you run a consultative discovery conversation, help each educator reach an honest fit decision, and enroll the ones the program genuinely serves.

Know what you'd be selling: a Master's degree our graduates consistently describe as transformative — for their teaching, their wellbeing, and their lives. Every enrollment you close is a teacher who stays in the profession stronger than they came to it. Most sales jobs ask you to believe in the product as a professional courtesy; this one earns it.

Three things to know about how we work, because they tell you whether this seat is for you:

You'd be joining an awesome team

This is a small group of mission-driven professionals who genuinely like each other and are unusually good at what they do. We chase a team goal — the number belongs to all of us, not to a leaderboard of individuals — so the incentive is to make the person next to you better. Reps trade what's working in real time, review each other's calls in the film room, and celebrate each other's wins loudly. If you've worked somewhere the top closer hoarded their tricks and the floor went quiet when someone was behind, this will feel different on day one.

We take selling seriously as a craft

Our motion is documented and built from what our best people actually do, not from theory — most of our wins close on the first substantive conversation, carried by disciplined follow-up. Everything we've built around it — the playbook, the coaching, the AI tooling — exists to get you to full speed fast: weeks, not quarters. After that, the book is yours to run. There are no individual volume quotas and no commission — we make sure you have a strong, steady set of calls, flexing up and down a bit during the highest-demand weeks and months, but overall protecting your calendar against getting overloaded. We hire people who run their own week, and then we get out of the way.

We sell with integrity, structurally

Teachers are trust professionals and our buyers for life — pressure tactics, false urgency, and manufactured scarcity don't just violate our values, they're incompatible with how we're regulated and how we retain students. Honest disqualification is a celebrated outcome. The product is what makes this possible: our graduates rate the program at an NPS in the +70s, so the honest conversation and the effective one are the same conversation. If your best work happens when you're allowed to tell a prospect the truth, you'll like it here.

What you'll actually do

  • Run ~8–12 scheduled discovery calls a day* (20 minutes each) with teachers who booked time to talk about the M.Ed. — assess fit, run real discovery, answer program and financing questions, and ask for the enrollment decision when the signal is there. *Daily volume fluctuates with seasonality, events, and experience.

  • Own the follow-up between calls: short, purposeful texting that protects shows and carries momentum, completion calls that finish decisions, and the follow-through that means nothing you promised a teacher ever slips.

  • Sell when teachers can talk. During the school year our calls concentrate in two windows: teachers' planning/lunch periods (roughly noon–2pm ET) and after school (roughly 4–8pm ET); in summer the weight shifts earlier. Your core coverage window is approximately noon–8pm ET on weekdays — in Central or Mountain time that's an ordinary late-morning-to-early-evening day, which is why we prefer those zones. Our best reps design their week around the teacher's clock on purpose; this role requires that design to be genuine and sustainable, not overtime.

  • Hand each newly enrolled educator cleanly to our onboarding team. Your job is the decision — a dedicated team carries students from deposit to day one, so your selling time stays selling time.

  • Bring what you learn back to the team: film-room participation, script feedback, sharing what's working. Our playbook carries our reps' wording because their wording works.

Who we're looking for

  • A proven consultative closer. 2+ years in a full-cycle closing role — high-consideration B2C (education, financial services, insurance, home services, coaching/wellness programs) or similar consultative sales — with a track record you can quantify and explain how it was measured.

  • One-conversation instincts. You know how to earn a decision in the first call when the fit is real — discovery first, then a direct, unapologetic ask — and how to walk away warmly when it isn't.

  • Follow-through as craft. You can describe the actual system you use to keep 100+ open conversations from slipping. Organized is table stakes; we're looking for someone who treats follow-up as the job, not the interruption.

  • A fast, eager tool adopter. This role runs on systems — a CRM (HubSpot a plus), AI-assisted call review and coaching, texting and scheduling tools, Google Workspace — and the stack keeps getting better. You don't just tolerate new tools; you pick them up quickly, fold them into how you work, and treat them as part of the craft.

  • A calendar owner. You manage your own energy and hours like a professional athlete — boundaries, blocks, evening selling by design, recovery budgeted after surges.

  • A teammate on purpose. Our reps get better in public — film-room reviews, script feedback, lending your wording to the playbook when it works. You want colleagues who sharpen your game and you return the favor; closers who guard their tricks don't thrive here.

  • Mission-resonant. You care that the thing you're selling genuinely changes teachers' lives, and you can say why in your own words. Our best closers are here on purpose — selling work that matters is the point.

You do NOT need admissions, higher-ed, or education-industry experience. We'll teach you the domain, the program, and the playbook — that's what our onboarding and coaching system is for. What we can't teach in eight weeks is professional selling. If you're a great closer who has always wanted your work to mean something, this is the seat.

Growth

This role has a real career ladder: EDC → Senior EDC, with promotion earned on craft, ownership, team impact, and judgment — assessed from your actual work, not tenure. Our most recent Senior promotion went to a rep whose calls became the film-room examples the team learns from. We promote from within on purpose.

Why this seat

Sales careers rarely offer all three: a product with real outcomes, a team of mission-driven professionals who treat selling as a craft worth studying and pull for each other, and a mission you'd defend at dinner. Teachers are holding up the hardest job in America, and the ones who find us are looking for a way to grow without leaving the classroom. You'd be the person who helps them decide well. If you've been waiting for a reason to bring your best selling somewhere it counts, this is it.

Compensation & benefits

  • Base salary: $80,000–$100,000, depending on experience and demonstrated track record

  • Equity eligibility (varies by experience)

  • Health, vision, and dental insurance

  • 401k and FSA/HSA eligibility

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Note: per our accreditation and Title IV compliance posture, compensation is never linked to enrollment counts — raises and promotions are earned on craft and professional factors. (Stated here because good salespeople always ask.)

How to apply

The application asks five short questions — they matter more than your résumé, and we read every answer.

Breathe for Change is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Compensation Range: $80K - $100K

  • The technical foundation. You can confidently interpret construction drawings, specifications, schedules, contracts, and project documentation across multiple disciplines. You understand how construction projects are planned, procured, and executed and can assess construction progress, contractor performance, and project risks through both documentation reviews and site observations.
  • The analytical and risk assessment capability. You can evaluate project budgets, pay applications, change orders, cost-to-complete forecasts, and supporting documentation to identify risks and assess project health.   • The communication and stakeholder management skills. You can build credibility with lenders, developers, contractors, consultants, and project teams.   • The independence and accountability. You thrive in a remote environment where autonomy, organization, and responsiveness are essential. jobs.excerpt: Work from anywhere, impact everywhere Diversity is at the heart of who we are at Xapo Bank.
jobs.description:
Work from anywhere, impact everywhere

Diversity is at the heart of who we are at Xapo Bank.
We’re a fully distributed team of over 160 Xapiens that work remotely from 50+ countries around the world.

Our beginning: A world that enjoys economic freedom and wealth protection,no matter where you live or who is running your country.
To achieve that, we search the world for the best people for the job.
We work hard, think globally, and inspire each other to learn and grow.
We are committed to changing the way things are done.

Although we are headquartered in Gibraltar, this is a full time, 100% remote position

Work from anywhere!

Position overview

We're looking for a Head of Quality Engineering to join our technology function, reporting directly to the CTO. At Xapo, we are building truly cross-functional teams with full ownership of design, architecture, building, testing, delivery, data, and operations, structured as Stream Aligned Teams (SATs), Platform teams and Enabling teams as per Team Topologies.

This role owns the quality framework across the entire technology function, coverage standards, gate criteria, AI-assisted test tooling, SAT enablement, and pre-release veto authority. You give engineering, apps, and web a single accountable owner for what "quality" means and how it is measured.

This is not a traditional QA role. You will not sit in a test team checking other people's code, SAT engineers own quality in their own code (shift-left). You own the system engineers test within: the framework, the tooling, the gates, and the standards.

The role is deliberately tooling-heavy over headcount-heavy. Your budget is for tooling and AI tokens, not for building a QA team beneath you. The agentic QA pipeline is already in active PoC with positive early results; you will own scaling it to production. Your north star: fully automated quality enforcement, where releases are blocked automatically when rigorous checks fail, without needing human intervention. Target: more than 80% of release quality decisions made by automated tooling within 12 months of hire.

This is an opportunity to shape how a regulated crypto bank defines and enforces software quality, at the intersection of engineering excellence, AI-assisted tooling, and a genuinely high-stakes production environment.

Responsibilities

  • Quality framework definition: own coverage standards (unit, service, integration, end-to-end), gate criteria, and the quality contribution to the function-level Definition of Done. Aligned with Head of Engineering on backend and Head of Frontend Engineering on client-side.
  • Coverage baselines: define measurable coverage thresholds per service and per tribe, with trend visibility, and drive adoption across teams.
  • Pre-release veto authority: hold and exercise the authority to block releases when quality gates are not met. Own the automated tooling that makes this veto self-triggering rather than dependent on a single person.
  • AI-assisted test tooling: define and drive the framework for automated test generation, regression coverage, integration test tooling, and the agentic QA pipeline. You are the designer and driver; implementation is a cross-functional effort with Platform, backend, web, and mobile engineers.
  • SAT enablement: produce the training, documentation, tooling, and templates that let Stream Aligned Team engineers do quality work themselves, without a separate QA function.
  • Test environment strategy: partner with Head of Platform Engineering on dedicated QA environments, test data management, and integration test infrastructure.
  • Quality posture reporting: own the metrics like defect escape rate, coverage trends, release veto rate, AI tooling adoption progress, and percentage of releases requiring no manual quality intervention.
  • Security testing integration: partner with Security on SAST, DAST, and dependency scanning as components of the quality gate.

Skills needed

  • 8+ years in software quality engineering, with a clear track record of owning quality frameworks across engineering organisations, not just managing a QA team or running manual test cycles.
  • Hands-on experience building CI/CD quality gates at multiple levels: unit, service, integration, and end-to-end. You know where tests go in a pipeline and how to make them block a release reliably.
  • Practical experience with AI-assisted test tooling, LLM-driven test generation, agentic QA pipelines, or equivalent. You don't need to have shipped a production-grade system, but you need a genuine point of view and hands-on exposure.
  • Demonstrated ability to raise quality standards without a reporting hierarchy, you have influenced engineering teams through better tooling, documentation, and frameworks, not through authority over people.
  • Solid understanding of distributed, event-driven microservices architectures and what testing them well requires: contract testing, consumer-driven contracts, integration test data strategies.
  • Experience defining and tracking quality metrics: defect escape rate, coverage baselines, release veto rates. You have turned quality into something measurable.
  • Strong written communication, you can write a coverage standard, gate criteria document, or enablement guide that engineers actually read and use.
  • Experience in regulated fintech, payments, or banking environments, with a strong emphasis on mobile-first product delivery. You have an appreciation for the stakes of a quality failure in a customer-funds context, particularly within the unique constraints and user expectations of a mobile application environment

Nice to have:

  • Hands-on experience with agentic or generative AI test tooling in production or near-production contexts.
  • Familiarity with Team Topologies, how Stream Aligned, Platform, and Enabling teams interact in practice.
  • Security testing experience: SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, and how these integrate into a CI/CD quality gate.
  • Background in crypto, Web3, custody, or blockchain-based systems.
  • Open-source contributions or external thought leadership (talks, articles, OSS projects) related to quality engineering or test automation.

While your North Star is absolute automation, you possess a "roll-up-your-sleeves" mentality. You aren't afraid to get your hands dirty, jump into the trenches, and manually test the mobile apps yourself if a critical release or an edge-case roadblock requires it.

Other requirements

  • A dedicated workspace.
  • A reliable internet connection with the fastest speed possible in your area.

jobs.title: Director, Security & Privacy (HIPAA Privacy & Security, HITECH Act requirements)
jobs.excerpt: Position OverviewThe Director, Security and Privacy leads HCUS’s enterprise security & privacy programs.
jobs.description:
Position Overview

The Director, Security and Privacy leads HCUS’s enterprise security & privacy programs. This role advises executive leadership on the security posture of the organization, including HCUS products, Cloud Services, HCUS business systems, and customer-facing technologies that process or store PHI.

The Director requires a strong understanding of organizational, product, cloud, and customer security, as well as the ability to communicate effectively with technical teams, business leaders, regulators, auditors, legal counsel, and customers’ C-suite executives. The Director works closely with HLUS Security and coordinates the activities of groups spanning all HCUS business units, and the Product Security Incident Response Team across HCUS, HLUS, and FTYO.

The Director provides guidance on information on security agreements, customer security requirements, regulatory obligations, and risk-management decisions. This role also plans and coordinates company resources to support compliance with HIPAA, SOC 2, applicable state and federal cybersecurity and privacy laws, and other relevant regulatory and contractual frameworks.

As the official HCUS HIPAA Privacy Officer and HIPAA Security Officer, the Director oversees the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of policies, procedures, safeguards, incident-response processes, and compliance activities designed to protect PHI and other sensitive information.

The role places equal emphasis on executing assigned responsibilities and coordinating with departments across the company, including HLUS and FTYO, to promote a consistent, integrated, risk-based approach to security and privacy. Through cross-functional collaboration, the Director supports the achievement of the organization’s short- and long-term security, privacy, and business objectives.

Company Overview

At FUJIFILM Healthcare Americas Corporation, we’re on a mission to innovate for a healthier world, and we need passionate, driven people like you to help us get there. Our cutting-edge healthcare solutions span diagnostic imaging, enterprise imaging, endoscopic and surgical imaging, as well as in-vitro diagnostics.

But we don’t stop at healthcare; our Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) team harnesses advanced radiography solutions to keep transportation infrastructure, aerospace, and oil and gas assets safe and running smoothly.

Ready to innovate, collaborate, and make a difference? Join us and bring your big ideas to life while working in a dynamic, flexible environment that fuels your creativity and drive.

Our headquarters is in Lexington, Massachusetts, an inspiring healthcare research hub in a historic town.

Fujifilm is globally headquartered in Tokyo with over 70,000 employees across four key business segments of healthcare, electronics, business innovation, and imaging. We are guided and united by our Group Purpose of “giving our world more smiles.” Visit:

Job Description

Duties and responsibilities

Privacy & Security Leadership

  • Serve as the organization’s designated HIPAA Security Officer and HIPAA Privacy Officer.
  • Develop, implement, maintain, and enforce the company’s information security, privacy, and program.
  • Establish and maintain a governance framework that supports compliance with HIPAA, HITECH, SOC 2, applicable state privacy laws, breach-notification requirements, contractual obligations, and other relevant healthcare and security standards.
  • Advise executive leadership on security, privacy, technology, and operational risks.
  • Present meaningful security, privacy, audit, and risk metrics to executive leadership and other stakeholders.
  • Maintain awareness of changes in healthcare privacy, cybersecurity, and regulatory requirements, translating those changes into actionable organizational improvements.

Policies, Procedures, and Program Management

  • Own the development, review, approval, implementation, and periodic revision of HCUS security and privacy policies, standards, procedures, and supporting documentation.
  • Ensure policies address administrative, physical, and technical safeguards appropriate to HCUS’s systems, workforce, operations, and risk profile.
  • Maintain required HIPAA documentation, including risk analyses, risk management plans, policies, training records, incident documentation, access reviews, vendor assessments, and compliance evidence.
  • Lead periodic program assessments and continuous improvement initiatives to measure and improve security and privacy maturity.

Risk Management and Security Assessments

  • Lead HCUS-wide security and privacy risk assessments, including HIPAA Security Rule risk analysis and periodic reassessments.
  • Identify, document, prioritize, and track remediation of security, privacy, operational, technical, and third-party risks.
  • Partner with Engineering, Product Management, HLUS Shared IT Services, Legal, and TAC teams to ensure security and privacy are incorporated into system design, software development, deployment, and operational processes.
  • Oversee vulnerability management, penetration testing, security testing, configuration reviews, access control reviews, and remediation tracking.
  • Ensure security controls are proportionate to HCUS’s risk profile and the sensitivity of PHI and other confidential information.

SOC 2, Audit, and Regulatory Readiness

  • Lead the HCUS’s SOC 2 program, including scoping, control design, evidence collection, readiness activities, auditor coordination, remediation management, and annual attestation efforts.
  • Coordinate internal and external audits, customer assessments, security questionnaires, and regulatory inquiries.
  • Maintain audit-ready evidence demonstrating operation of security and privacy controls.
  • Monitor compliance with contractual commitments, Business Associate Agreements (BAAs), customer security requirements, and data protection obligations.
  • Partner with internal teams and external advisors to address audit findings, corrective action plans, and compliance gaps.

Incident Response and Breach Management

  • Continuously develop, maintain, test, and improve the HCUS’s security incident response and breach-response plans.
  • Lead or coordinate response activities for suspected or confirmed security incidents, privacy incidents, and PHI breaches.
  • Ensure incidents are appropriately investigated, documented, contained, remediated, and reviewed.
  • Coordinate with leadership, legal counsel, technical teams, customers, insurers, and other stakeholders as appropriate during significant incidents.
  • Support breach-risk assessment and notification decision-making in accordance with HIPAA, state law, contractual requirements, and company policy.
  • Conduct post-incident reviews and ensure corrective actions are assigned, tracked, and completed.

Technical Security Oversight

  • Partner with technical leadership to oversee the security architecture and safeguards protecting cloud environments, applications, endpoints, networks, identities, integrations, and data.
  • Support implementation and operation of controls such as identity and access management, multi-factor authentication, encryption, logging and monitoring, secure configuration management, vulnerability management, backup and recovery, and business continuity capabilities.
  • Promote secure software development lifecycle practices, including security requirements, code review, dependency management, security testing, threat modeling, and release controls.
  • Ensure appropriate protections for medical imaging data, DICOM workflows, integrations, APIs, interoperability platforms, and connected customer environments.

Vendor, Customer, and Third-Party Risk Management

  • Establish and oversee a third-party risk management program for vendors, subcontractors, cloud service providers, and other business partners that may access, process, transmit, or store PHI or other sensitive data.
  • Review security and privacy due diligence materials, including SOC reports, penetration testing summaries, certifications, data protection terms, and business continuity documentation.
  • Ensure appropriate contractual safeguards, including BAAs and security requirements, are in place before third-party access to PHI or sensitive systems is granted.
  • Support customer due diligence requests, security reviews, and discussions with customer information security, privacy, procurement, and compliance teams.

Workforce Education and Culture

  • Develop and administer security and privacy awareness training for all HCUS members.
  • Ensure role-based training is provided to employees and contractors with specialized responsibilities or access to PHI, production systems, or sensitive information.
  • Foster a culture of security, privacy, accountability, and timely incident reporting across HCUS.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Security, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Healthcare Administration, Privacy, Risk Management, or a related field; equivalent experience may be considered.
  • 7+ years of progressive experience in information security, privacy, compliance, risk management, healthcare technology, or related discipline.
  • 3+ years of experience leading or managing security, privacy, compliance, or governance programs.
  • Demonstrated experience with HIPAA Privacy Rule, HIPAA Security Rule, HITECH Act requirements, and healthcare breach response.
  • Experience leading SOC 2 readiness, audits, control implementation, and evidence management.
  • Experience conducting risk assessments, developing risk treatment plans, and managing remediation activities.
  • Experience developing and maintaining incident response, business continuity, and disaster recovery processes.
  • Strong knowledge of common security frameworks and standards, such as NIST Cybersecurity Framework, NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-66, CIS Controls, ISO 27001, and SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria.
  • Familiarity with cloud security, SaaS application security, identity and access management, encryption, logging/monitoring, secure software development practices, and vendor risk management.
  • Ability to communicate complex security, privacy, and regulatory concepts effectively to technical teams, customers, executives, and non-technical workforce members.
  • Strong judgment, organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage sensitive and confidential matters.

Preferred requirements

  • Experience in a healthcare SaaS, medical imaging, health IT, clinical informatics, PACS, RIS, DICOM, interoperability, or medical device-adjacent environment
  • Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC, HCISPP, CHPC, CHC, CHSP, CIPM, CIPP/US, or equivalent.
  • Experience with HITRUST, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, FDA cybersecurity considerations, or state healthcare privacy regulations.
  • Experience managing customer security assessments and enterprise healthcare customer requirements.
  • Experience with cloud environments such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform.
  • Familiarity with security operations, SIEM/logging platforms, endpoint protection, vulnerability scanning, and cloud security posture management tools.

Physical requirements

The position requires the ability to perform the following physical demands and/or have the listed capabilities:

  • The ability to sit up 75-100% of applicable work
  • The ability to use your hands and fingers to feel and manipulate items, including keyboards, up to 100% of applicable work time.
  • The ability to stand, talk, and hear for 75% of applicable work
  • The ability to lift and carry up to ten pounds up to 20% of applicable work
  • Close Vision: The ability to see clearly at twenty inches or less.

Travel

  • Occasional (up to 25%) travel may be required based on business

Salary and Benefits

  • $134,406.00 to $186,696.00
  • Medical, Dental, Vision
  • Life Insurance
  • 401K
  • Paid Time Off

jobs.excerpt: About the RoleOur client is a specialist UK-based business operating within the asset finance sector.
jobs.description:
About the Role

Our client is a specialist UK-based business operating within the asset finance sector. They are looking for a highly articulate and commercially aware LinkedIn Appointment Setter / Cold Messaging Specialist to support their business development activity.

This is not a high-volume, copy-and-paste outreach position.

The successful candidate will be responsible for conducting carefully researched LinkedIn outreach, building relationships with senior professionals within the finance sector, generating strong response rates, and ultimately booking qualified meetings for the company’s directors.

The business operates in a highly relationship-driven and reputation-sensitive market. For that reason, outreach needs to feel personalised, credible and consultative rather than aggressive or sales-led.

The role would suit someone who genuinely understands how to use LinkedIn as a relationship-building and appointment-setting platform and can explain not only what they are doing, but why a particular outreach strategy is likely to work.

Requirements

Key Responsibilities

  • Conduct approximately 50 high-quality, personalised LinkedIn outreach messages per day.
  • Research prospects before making contact and tailor messaging accordingly.
  • Build rapport with senior professionals across the asset finance and broader financial services sectors.
  • Re-engage prospects who may already have an existing relationship or previous conversation with the directors.
  • Generate strong response rates from LinkedIn outreach.
  • Convert conversations into qualified appointments for the company’s directors.
  • Manage LinkedIn connection requests strategically and consistently.
  • Develop appropriate messaging sequences for different prospect types.
  • Follow up with prospects in a professional and natural manner.
  • Engage with relevant prospects' LinkedIn content where appropriate to increase familiarity and strengthen relationships.
  • Maintain accurate records of outreach activity, responses and appointments.
  • Review outreach performance and adapt messaging based on results.
  • Communicate the strategy behind different approaches and demonstrate commercial reasoning.
  • Initially submit messaging and outreach strategies for approval while learning the company’s tone of voice.
  • Gradually take greater ownership of conversations once trust and consistency have been established.
  • Learn how the directors communicate and ensure messages sound authentic and aligned with the company.
  • Potentially manage outreach through a director's LinkedIn account once sufficient trust has been established.

What the Client Is Looking For

The client is looking for someone considerably stronger than a basic administrator or junior appointment setter.

They want someone who understands that successful LinkedIn outreach is about credibility, research, positioning and communication, rather than simply sending large numbers of messages.

Finance Sector Experience

Previous experience working within financial services, finance recruitment, banking, asset finance or another finance-related environment is highly desirable and considered important for this role.

Candidates do not necessarily need direct asset finance experience, but they should be comfortable communicating with professionals working in a sophisticated financial environment.

Strong LinkedIn Knowledge

LinkedIn will be the primary platform used in the role.

The ideal candidate will already have:

  • A professional and credible LinkedIn profile.
  • A good understanding of LinkedIn networking.
  • Experience conducting direct outreach.
  • Knowledge of connection-building strategies.
  • An understanding of how profile credibility influences response rates.
  • Experience generating conversations and meetings through LinkedIn.

A strong existing LinkedIn presence would be particularly advantageous.

Strategic Thinking

The client does not simply want someone who follows instructions.

They want someone capable of looking at a prospect and deciding:

  • Why should we approach this person?
  • What will make them respond?
  • What angle should we use?
  • What previous relationship or information can we reference?
  • Should we message them immediately or build familiarity first?
  • How should we follow up?
  • Why is this approach likely to work?

Candidates must therefore be able to demonstrate strategic thinking alongside execution.

Excellent Written Communication

The company's market is highly relationship-driven.

Messages must therefore be:

  • Professional.
  • Natural.
  • Concise.
  • Articulate.
  • Personalised.
  • Commercially intelligent.
  • Appropriate for senior finance professionals.

The client wants outreach that feels like the continuation of a genuine business conversation rather than traditional cold prospecting.

Results Focus

Performance will primarily be assessed on:

  • LinkedIn response rates.
  • Quality of conversations generated.
  • Number of qualified appointments booked.
  • Overall effectiveness of outreach strategies.

The successful candidate should therefore be comfortable working towards clear measurable outcomes.

Attention to Detail

This is a quality-over-quantity role.

Rather than sending thousands of automated messages, the expectation is approximately 50 well-considered messages each day.

Candidates need to be thorough, organised and capable of researching prospects before contacting them.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The strongest candidate is likely to have:

  • Previous LinkedIn outreach or appointment-setting experience.
  • Exposure to financial services or another professional services environment.
  • Excellent written English.
  • Strong commercial awareness.
  • Confidence communicating with senior professionals.
  • Excellent attention to detail.
  • Strong research skills.
  • Experience generating appointments through written outreach.
  • A credible and professional LinkedIn presence.
  • An analytical mindset and interest in improving response rates.
  • The ability to understand and reproduce another person's communication style.
  • The confidence to recommend different outreach approaches rather than simply waiting for instructions.
  • A trustworthy and dependable working style.

Benefits

Location: Remote – South Africa

Salary: £1,600–£1,700 per month

Employment: Full-time

Primary Platform: LinkedIn

jobs.excerpt: About Merlin: Merlin (NASDAQ: MRLN) is a publicly traded aerospace and defense company building a non-human pilot to deliver full-stack autonomy for any aircraft from takeoff to touchdown.
jobs.description:
About Merlin:

Merlin (NASDAQ: MRLN) is a publicly traded aerospace and defense company building a non-human pilot to deliver full-stack autonomy for any aircraft from takeoff to touchdown. The Merlin Pilot autonomy system powers a growing range of aircraft and mission profiles and has been proven through hundreds of autonomous flights from Merlin's global flight test facilities, including Kerikeri, New Zealand; Quonset Point, Rhode Island; and soon, Bedford, Massachusetts. Headquartered in Boston, Merlin is expanding its organization to accelerate the development and deployment of its autonomy platform, helping customers solve some of aviation's most pressing challenges, from pilot shortages to improving flight safety. Backed by some of the world's leading investors prior to its public listing, Merlin continues to advance the certification and commercialization of autonomous flight across commercial and defense aviation.

About You:

This role pairs deep, personal expertise in civil certification with the people leadership needed to manage two additional, interdependent certification disciplines: military airworthiness and cyber security certification. You are a proven certification leader with extensive, hands-on experience managing complex civil certification programs through FAA Part 23 and Part 25, EASA CS-23 and CS-25, and foreign validations. You also bring working experience in military airworthiness through MIL-HDBK-516C and MIL-STD-882E compliance. You understand the process rigor and collaborative relationships required to achieve airworthiness approvals across civil and military domains, and how airborne cyber security assurance requirements must be part of the initial design concepts on every new program. You lead by building relationships within the organization and externally with regulators, sponsoring offices, and your own team of certification leads, and you know how to translate emerging and often ambiguous guidance into a defensible, schedule-compatible certification strategy.
Merlin Labs builds autonomous aviation systems for civil and defense customers, and the engineering organization behind that work needs a leader who is personally expert in civil certification and who can manage the work of the military airworthiness lead and Cyber Certification Lead. You will own civil certification (FAA Part 23 and Part 25) directly, while leading the military airworthiness lead and cyber certification lead and their teams, reporting to the VP of Airworthiness & certification. If you want to grow and lead the certification and airworthiness teams that enable Merlin to field robust, certifiable autonomous systems to civil and defense customers on a demanding schedule, this is the role for you.

Responsibilities:

  • Support current New Zealand CAANZ certification activities for the U.S. based aspects and lead Merlin's civil certification strategy with the FAA and other foreign authorities, serving as primary technical authority and primary liaison with regulatory authorities for U.S. certifications.
  • Manage all aspects of new civil certification projects: Core process standardization, A&C initial assessments, compliance strategies and A & C plans, issue papers and risk assessments, and guide the Merlin team to final compliance.
  • Lead and grow the Military Airworthiness and Cyber Certification teams, setting priorities, establishing and standardizing core processes, mentoring, and reviewing technical work while the team executes day-to-day military airworthiness and cyber certification activities.
  • Oversee the military airworthiness certification strategy for Merlin's defense programs through the Military Airworthiness Lead, serving as an escalation point to mitigate technical, resource, and capability risks.
  • Oversee closure of Military Certification Review Items (MCRIs), Issue Papers, and related airworthiness documentation through the Military Airworthiness Lead, ensuring compliance with MIL-HDBK-516C, MIL-STD-882E, applicable DEF STANs, and JSSG guidance.
  • Oversee the cyber security certification strategy across civil and military programs through the Cyber Certification Lead, driving integration of airborne cyber security assurance activities with existing safety and development assurance processes and serve as an escalation point to mitigate technical, resource, capability risks.
  • Partner with the process assurance manager and engineering discipline leads to integrate civil certification, military airworthiness, and cyber security certification processes with Merlin's broader process assurance and configuration management framework.
  • Drive continuous improvement of civil certification, military airworthiness, and cyber security certification processes based on audit findings, program lessons learned, and evolving regulatory and DoD guidance.
  • Report to the VP of Airworthiness & certification on program health for civil certification and military airworthiness projects as well as the process improvement roadmap across all three disciplines.
  • Build scalable, repeatable civil certification, military airworthiness, and cyber security frameworks to ensure the success of all three functions as Merlin adds civil and defense programs to their portfolio.

Qualifications:

  • Direct, hands-on experience achieving FAA Part 23 and/or Part 25 type certificates, amendments, or Supplemental Type Certificates, including EASA CS-23/CS-25 or other foreign validation experience.
  • Bachelor’s degree in aerospace engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field; master’s degree in a related field preferred.
  • Minimum of 12+ years of aerospace certification experience, including significant exposure to FAA and foreign certification processes and 5+ years of experience leading or managing a team of engineers, including hiring, mentoring, and performance management across technical disciplines.
  • Proven ability to lead certification efforts for complex new or novel aircraft technologies: interfacing directly with regulatory authorities and managing certification projects from establishment of certification basis, resolution of issue papers and risk assessments, through certification closure or airworthiness approval.
  • Strong leadership and project management capabilities in cross-functional environments.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to produce high-quality certification documentation.
  • Experience with designee appointment and management processes and Organization Designation Authorization (ODA) management.
  • Strong working knowledge of 14 CFR Part 21, 23, 25, and 183.
  • Familiarity in 14 CFR Part 43 and 145 procedures and Part 91 and 135 operations.
  • Working knowledge of:
  • Systems engineering principles — requirements decomposition, V&V planning, and configuration management.
  • Software and hardware assurance standards (DO-178C, DO-254, MIL-STD-882).
  • Safety assessment methodologies: FHA, FMEA/FMECA, FTA, common cause analysis.
  • Airworthiness standards relevant to military platforms — MIL-SPECs, MIL-STDs, JSSG-2001, and MIL-HDBK-516.
  • DoD cybersecurity and information assurance frameworks (e.g., RMF, NIST SP 800-53, CMMC) as they apply to airborne systems and Controlled Unclassified Information on defense programs.
  • Airborne cyber security assurance standards (DO-326A/ED-202A, DO-356A/ED-203A) and how cyber security risk assessments integrate with ARP4754A/ARP4761A safety processes
  • Emerging aerospace technologies such as UAVs or advanced air mobility.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience with ASTM F3230 and F3061 consensus standards, or other Part 23 / consensus-based certification bases relevant to small and autonomous aircraft.
  • Background in autonomous or unmanned aviation systems (UAS/UAV).
  • Prior experience in military operational environments.
  • Familiarity with machine learning-based software assurance and its intersection with cyber security certification.
  • Experience building or scaling certification functions in a growing company.
  • Experience in AI applications used in standardization of processes, procedures and requirements.
Merlin Labs offers an innovative, entrepreneurial, and team-focused startup environment. We also offer a top-notch benefits package (health, dental, life, unlimited vacation, and 401k with match) and work/life integration. Being part of the Merlin team allows you to become part of a small team that supports professional development while working together to achieve our mission.

We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, genetic information, sex (including pregnancy), gender, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, military service or obligation or disability status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Who You’ll Work With

As a Layer1 software engineer, you will get to work on software that manages the physical layer, where packets meet the outside world. Stable and reliable physical connectivity is critical for any network and that is your challenge. You will get to write control software that brings to life everything from the ubiquitous 1GBASE-T connectors to 400G long reach optics that provide fiber connectivity across continents. Your software will need to work across a wide variety of forwarding engines, connectors and interface chips called gearboxes, which allow our hardware platforms to support diverse physical connectivity options within a product family. You will build instrumentation and telemetry tools that track physical link health parameters reported by the Layer1 components and enable operators to monitor and troubleshoot their links effectively. You will also work closely with our Optics teams to define standards for new media and bring them to market.

Arista Software Engineering roles demand a strong and broad software engineering background. While the primary focus area for this role is Layer1 software, the role will cover all aspects of software development spanning the addition of new features, debugging problems and fine tuning code for scalability and performance. You will own your projects from definition to deployment and customer interactions, and you will be responsible for the quality of everything you deliver.

Arista Software Engineering prides itself on a supportive and growth oriented culture. Over time, as your interests change, coupled with evolving business needs you will have the opportunity to switch from Layer1 to other areas, if you like.

What You’ll Do

  • Interface with customers, product management and hardware engineers to come up with innovative new Layer1 features.
  • Architect, design and manage the development of these features.
  • Develop and maintain features using C, C++ and Python, review and contribute to functional and design specifications. Build automated tests and test infrastructure to test the features.
  • Work with hardware and manufacturing teams to bring new Layer1 components like Phys and Transceivers to market.
  • Collaborate with hardware engineers to design optimal software control interfaces for managing Layer1 components.
  • Provide technical leadership across features, projects and tools.
  • Work with Customer Support Engineers and customers to analyze, mitigate and fix problems in customer networks.
  • Work with the System Test Engineers to analyze problems found in their tests and provide fixes for those problems.
  • Mentor new and junior engineers to bring them up to speed in Arista's software development environment.
  • BS Computer Science/Electrical Engineering/Computer Engineering + 3 years experience, or equivalent work experience
  • Expert knowledge of C or C++ and Python.
  • Knowledge of UNIX or Linux
  • Knowledge of digital communication technologies like modulation and signal encoding schemes is a plus.
  • Understanding of IP networking and/or distributed systems is a plus
  • Experience working with low level hardware components is a plus
  • Applied understanding of software engineering principles
  • Strong problem solving and software troubleshooting skills
  • Ability to design a solution and implement features independently.
  • Ability to work in small teams.

Arista Networks is an industry leader in data-driven, client-to-cloud networking for large data center, campus and routing environments. What sets us apart is our relentless pursuit of innovation. Position Summary

Radiology Associates of South Florida (RASF)is seeking a radiologist to join our Emergency Radiology division. H1B or J1 Visa sponsorships welcome! As part of a dynamic, multi-specialty practice, you will work alongside a team of exceptional professionals, providing high-quality imaging services to Baptist Health South Florida, one of the nation’s leading healthcare systems.
